entities.name: Gabriel proposes a hypothetical revision of Dog Day Afternoon
entities.description: Gabriel suggests an alternate version of the film 'Dog Day Afternoon' where the robbers escalate by killing hostages, challenging the others to consider how media coverage and public response would change under modern conditions.

entities.name: Roberts critiques Gabriel's movie idea as commercially unviable
entities.description: Roberts expresses skepticism about the success of Gabriel's film concept, arguing that audiences prefer happy endings, implying the idea would not resonate with mainstream viewers.

entities.name: Stanley rejects the idea of the protagonist escaping successfully
entities.description: Stanley shakes his head when asked if Pacino's character should escape with the money, indicating that the 'bad guy can't win' due to the moral structure expected in storytelling.

entities.name: Gabriel concludes the conversation and prepares to leave
entities.description: After reflecting on the discussion, Gabriel checks his watch, comments on the lifelessness of the place, and announces his departure from the booth.
